fields.label: Default Company
fields.description: Used on new plans, assignments and payments. Falls back to the site's own default company when empty.
Comma-separated keywords. Warehouses whose name contains any of these are hidden from the block picker (e.g. Store, Mill, Tank).
fields.label: Block Exclude Keywords
Only work the Farms listed below
fields.description: Off: every farm in Upande Core is available, and the table below only supplies cost projects and area overrides. On: the screens offer just the farms listed. Off by default, so adding a row to give a farm its cost project never hides the others.

fields.label: Only show each person the Farms they are permitted
fields.description:
On: the farm list every screen offers is narrowed to the farms this person holds a Frappe User Permission for, and a person with no such permission still sees every farm -- Frappe's own default. Off, the default, is exactly today's behaviour on every site.

Run the audit before turning this on. It reports who would lose access and who has already been working farms they are not permitted:

    bench --site <site> execute work_management.farm_permission_audit.print_report

Anybody it lists as working outside their permission is either mis-permissioned or the permission is wrong, and that has to be settled by a person before this is switched on -- otherwise the fix looks like an outage.

One row per farm this project works: its cost project — which is where a plan's activities come from — and an area override where the farm's own area is not the figure to divide by. The farms themselves are Upande Core's records. Whether this list also narrows the screens is the checkbox above.
fields.label: Farms in use
Time & Attendance integration
fields.description: Each check blocks assigning work / recording actuals for a conflicting employee, with an explicit logged override. Toggle each independently.

fields.label: Check attendance (block employees marked Absent)
fields.description: Blocks when a submitted Attendance record says Absent on the date. Missing attendance never blocks.

fields.label: Check approved leaves
fields.description: Blocks when an approved Leave Application covers the date(s).

fields.label: Check weekly offs / holidays
fields.description: Actuals: blocks recording work on the employee's off day. Assigner: flags only when offs cover the whole assignment window.

fields.label: Require a morning scan for day-of assignment
fields.description: When an assignment window includes today (and the cutoff has passed), workers with no biometric scan and no Present attendance today need an override. Night-shift workers are exempt.

fields.label: Show today's presence on the assigner
fields.description: On: each worker on the assigner carries a chip for today — P with the scan time when an Employee Checkin or a submitted Attendance says they are on site, A when marked Absent, ? when there is neither. Off by default, because a site without biometric hardware or with attendance kept elsewhere gets ? on every worker, which reads as information and is not. Off, the reads do not run.

fields.label: Morning scan cutoff
fields.description: Before this time, missing scans are shown as a grey chip only — no override dialog.

fields.label: Check scans when recording actuals
fields.description: Recording a quantity for a worker with zero biometric scans and no Present attendance on that work date needs an override.

fields.label: Off-day rule when assigning
fields.options:
Entire window
Any off day
Ignore at assignment
fields.description: Entire window: only flag a worker whose off days cover the WHOLE assignment period. Any off day: flag any off day inside the period. Ignore: off days never flag at assignment (actuals still checks the exact day).

fields.label: Paid on marked-Absent days
fields.description: Flags a paid day where attendance says the worker was Absent. Days whose attendance was later corrected are never flagged.

fields.label: No presence evidence at all (no scan, no attendance)
fields.description: Flags a paid day with no biometric scan and no attendance record of any kind.

fields.label: Earning while on approved leave
fields.description: Flags a paid day that falls inside an approved leave application.

fields.label: Work recorded on off days / holidays
fields.description: Flags work recorded on a weekly off or a holiday. Legitimate when overtime was deliberate.

fields.label: Amount doesn't match qty × rate
fields.description: Flags a row whose amount is not quantity times rate — usually an edited or corrupted value.

fields.label: Two Farms, one day
fields.description: Flags a worker paid on two farms for the same day.

fields.label: Entered and approved by the same person
fields.description: Flags work entered and approved by the same person, so nothing had an independent check.

fields.label: Earning after leaving the job
fields.description: Flags earnings dated after the worker's leaving date.

fields.label: Recorded work with no pay (zero-valued rows)
fields.description: Flags rows valued at zero although the document carries a rate. Repairable in one click.

fields.label: Paid twice for the same day (duplicate entries)
fields.description: Flags the same worker, task and date recorded in two documents. Repairable in one click, keeping the earliest copy.

fields.label: Left the company but still on live assignments
fields.description: Flags employees who have left but are still on live assignments.

fields.label: More hours recorded than the day is long
fields.description: Flags a worker whose recorded hours across every task on one date exceed that date's standard day. Judged per date, so two ordinary full days are never read as one long one. Sometimes real overtime; often a split day whose halves were both left at the full standard.

fields.label: Hours and output disagree
fields.description: Flags a row whose output runs well ahead of the time recorded against it — three hours producing a full day's target. Not a short day: four hours producing about half a target is an ordinary half day and is never flagged.

fields.label: Hourly task where the quantity and the hours differ
fields.description: On a task measured in Hours the quantity and the hours are the same fact typed twice. Flags the rows where they disagree — one of the two is wrong, and the quantity is the one that pays.

fields.label: Auto-release inactive employees from assignments
fields.description: When ON: deactivating an employee in HR marks their Active rows on live assignments as Left (dated today) with a comment on each assignment.

fields.label: Consultant users (comma-separated emails)
fields.description: Superseded by Stage Approvers rows on the Planner: Weekly Consultant stage. Read-only, and removed in the next release.

fields.label: Master plan post-approval editors (comma-separated emails)
fields.description: Who may correct a master plan after it is approved. Empty means nobody, which is the default. System Manager is deliberately not swept in — an administrator who must intervene already has the Desk form.

fields.label: Allow more than one approved master plan per Farm at a time
fields.description:
Off: a farm holds one approved budget for any given day, and approving a second plan whose period overlaps is refused. On: a farm may run two budgets over the same days — separate streams of work, each with its own ceiling.

Raising an overlapping plan has always been allowed and is reported when it happens; this governs approval. Nothing is bypassed silently: the approver is still told which plan overlaps, because raising the same plan twice by mistake looks identical to raising a deliberate second one.

Each request already records the plan it draws down, so the planner asks which budget when two cover the dates rather than guessing. Off by default — a site that has always run one budget per period keeps doing so.

fields.label: A worker's day
fields.description: How long a full day is, and whether one worker's day may be shared between two tasks. The hours are the denominator every man-day figure divides by, and the default is what this code has always assumed.

fields.label: Allow a worker's day to be split between tasks
fields.description:
Off: a worker already on a live assignment over these dates cannot be put on another one, which is how it has always worked.

On: they can. Release them from one task's crew — their recorded work and pay stay exactly as they are — and assign them to another, recording work against both on the same day. Hours are then typed on each row, so the day counts once however many tasks it spanned.

Off by default: with it off no figure on any site changes.

fields.label: Standard hours, Monday to Friday
fields.description: What a full weekday is. Man-days divide by this, so a worker who gave four of eight hours is half a man-day.

fields.label: Standard hours, Saturday
fields.description: Six by default. A full six-hour Saturday is a whole man-day, not three quarters of one.

fields.label: Standard hours, Sunday
fields.description: Sunday is worked on these farms, so it is a full day by default. Set it to zero for a site that does not work Sundays — a zero day contributes no man-days rather than dividing by nothing.

fields.label: Rates
fields.description: Task rates are effective-dated in Work Task Rate. Task.custom_rate is mirrored from whichever period is active today, so the Task list stays the place you edit rates day to day — an edit there is recorded as a period starting today. Backdated changes belong to a rate card.
The daily wage most active rate periods are derived from. Read-only — change it by applying a rate card, not by typing here.
fields.label: Current Daily Wage
Rate Coverage
fields.options: Coverage, borderline tasks awaiting a decision and the last run are loaded by the Rates buttons above.

fields.label: Recalculate from a date
fields.description: Revalues UNPAID day-rows at the rate in force on each work date. Never touches paid rows, tasks that are not wage-derived, or tasks whose unit or daily target changed at the boundary. Always dry-run it first.
Revalue work dated on or after this day, e.g. 2026-07-21 for the 340 → 387 rate card.
fields.label: Recalculate From

fields.description: Optional upper bound. Leave empty to run to the latest recorded work.
fields.label: Recalculate To

fields.description: Leave empty for all farms.
fields.label: Farm Scope

fields.description: On: report what would change and write nothing. Turn this off only after reading the dry-run figures.
fields.label: Dry Run
Last Run
fields.description: The Work Rate Recalc Run document the last recalculation wrote. Set by the system.

fields.label: Last Run On
fields.description: When the last recalculation ran. Set by the system.

fields.label: Last Run By
fields.description: Who ran the last recalculation. Set by the system.

fields.label: Last Run Summary
fields.description: What the last recalculation changed. Set by the system.

fields.label: Payroll
fields.description: Sending a worker to accounts creates a submitted Additional Salary against this component, so payroll picks the earnings up on the next salary slip.

fields.label: Salary Component
fields.description: Earning component the Additional Salary is raised against. Leave empty to stop Additional Salary records being created.

fields.label: Who this system pays
fields.description: This system pays task work only. Salaried staff are paid through payroll, so their recorded work must never become a payment here. An employee qualifies if ANY of the three lists below matches — that way a blank employment type on a new hire does not quietly make them unpayable.

fields.label: Employment types paid here
fields.description: Pick them. Anyone whose employment type is listed is paid per unit.

fields.label: Employment types paid here (old, typed)
fields.description: Superseded by the picker above. Still read when the picker is empty, so nothing changes until you fill it in; it will be removed once every site has.

fields.label: Designations paid here
fields.description: Pick them. Any one of these three lists matching is enough.

fields.label: Designations paid here (old, typed)
fields.description: Superseded by the picker above. Still read when the picker is empty, so nothing changes until you fill it in; it will be removed once every site has.

fields.label: Categories paid here
fields.description: Pick them. Category is a Select on Employee, so these are chosen from the same options rather than linked.

fields.label: Categories paid here (old, typed)
fields.description: Superseded by the picker above. Still read when the picker is empty, so nothing changes until you fill it in; it will be removed once every site has.

fields.label: Allow sending the week still in progress
fields.description: Off: a pay week can only be sent once it closes, so a week is never paid twice. On: the current week can be sent for the days worked so far.

fields.options:
Monday
Tuesday
Wednesday
Thursday
Friday
Saturday
Sunday
fields.label: Pay week starts on
fields.description: The weekday a pay week opens. Default Sunday. Together with the closing day this decides how work is grouped into weekly payments.

fields.options:
Monday
Tuesday
Wednesday
Thursday
Friday
Saturday
Sunday
fields.label: Pay week ends on
fields.description: The weekday a pay week closes. Default Saturday. If the span is shorter than seven days, the weekdays left over belong to no week at all and cannot be sent unless single-day sending is on.

fields.options:
Monday
Tuesday
Wednesday
Thursday
Friday
Saturday
Sunday
fields.label: Pay day
fields.description: The weekday payment is expected. Defaults to the closing day.

fields.label: Also allow sending a chosen range of days
fields.description: Pay weeks can always be sent -- one payment per worker per completed week, which is what payroll has always received. Tick this to additionally offer paying a range you choose: one day, five days, a fortnight, up to a month. The range is grouped from the first date selected rather than into pay weeks, so it can pay a weekday the pay week above leaves out, which cannot be sent weekly at all. Ticking this changes nothing on its own -- an ordinary send still groups into pay weeks.

fields.label: Capabilities
fields.description:
Who may do each thing the screens allow, beyond approving. Approving is set by the Approval Steps below; this covers the rest -- raising a budget, changing a rate, sending a payment run, entering work.

One row per capability per role. Add a second row with the same capability to grant it to another role. A capability with no row at all falls back to System Manager, so a site part-way through being configured is never locked out.

These used to be lists inside the code, naming one company's job titles, so a farm could say who approves a plan and not who may change a rate.

fields.label: Approvals
fields.description: Every step of every approval chain, and who takes it. The stages are fixed by the app; the role and the people are yours. Switching a stage off relinks the chain so the step before it approves straight through to the next one. Saving here regenerates the workflows.

fields.label: Approval Stages
fields.description: One row per step of every approval chain, seeded on install. The step and its document are fixed; set the role that takes it, and clear On to drop the step and relink the chain around it. Submit steps cannot be switched off.

fields.label: Stage Approvers
fields.description: One row per person per stage. Leave Farm empty for someone who approves every farm. On a farm-scoped stage, give each farm its own role override to stop one farm's manager approving another's.

fields.label: Header Logo
fields.description: Shown in the header of the five work screens. Leave empty for the module's own wordmark.

fields.label: Taxonomy
fields.description: What this installation calls the levels work is organised by. Leave a name empty to use the built-in wording. Changing a name relabels the desk forms and the work screens; it never changes data.

fields.label: Use a level above the farm
fields.description: Names the level above the farm, for Employee records and for reports. Farms themselves are Upande Core's records and carry no business unit of their own.

fields.label: Level above the farm (singular)
fields.description: Default: Business Unit.

fields.label: Level above the farm (plural)
fields.description: Default: Business Units.

fields.label: Farm level (singular)
fields.description: Default: Farm. Estate, site, division — whatever your project calls it.

fields.label: Farm level (plural)
fields.description: Default: Farms.

fields.label: Block level (singular)
fields.description: Default: Block. The piece of ground work is planned against.

fields.label: Block level (plural)
fields.description: Default: Blocks.

fields.label: Cost grouping (singular)
fields.description: Default: Section. Names the grouping the cost-centre view can be switched to, and the toggle that switches it.

fields.label: Cost grouping (plural)
fields.description: Default: Sections.
